questions.name: Remote Identification
questions.objective: 3.1 Remote ID applicability and broadcast requirements
questions.text: A remote pilot is reviewing the broadcast requirements under 14 CFR Part 89 to ensure their Standard Remote ID sUAS is transmitting the correct information during flight. Which set of data elements must a Standard Remote ID sUAS broadcast throughout its operation?

answers.text: Only the UAS serial number and the geographic coordinates of the control station at one-second intervals
The UAS identity (serial number or session ID), latitude and longitude of the UA and control station, altitude of both, velocity, and a timestamp
Only the operator's FAA-issued registration number and the aircraft's current groundspeed and heading
The aircraft's make, model, maximum takeoff weight, and the operator's Part 107 certificate number

explanations.a: Broadcasting only the serial number and control station coordinates omits required elements such as aircraft altitude, velocity, and timestamp; the broadcast must be more comprehensive.
explanations.b: Under 14 CFR 89.305, a Standard Remote ID UAS must broadcast the UAS's unique identifier, the latitude and longitude and altitude of both the UA and the control station, the velocity of the UA, and a time mark, among other required elements.
explanations.c: The registration number and groundspeed alone do not satisfy the Standard Remote ID broadcast requirement; the full set of elements defined in 89.305 is required.
explanations.d: Make, model, and certificate number are not Remote ID broadcast elements; the broadcast is real-time positional and operational data, not static aircraft description data.

questions.name: Remote Identification
questions.objective: 3.1 Remote ID applicability and broadcast requirements
questions.keyword: Remote ID broadcast initiation and termination
questions.text: A remote pilot operating a Standard Remote ID sUAS wants to understand precisely when the Remote ID broadcast must be active. Under 14 CFR Part 89, from what point to what point must the Remote ID broadcast be continuously transmitted?

answers.text: From the moment the aircraft is powered on until it is powered off, including any time spent on the ground between flights
Only during portions of the flight when the sUAS is operating within controlled airspace where ATC monitoring is required
From takeoff until the sUAS lands and comes to a complete stop at the conclusion of the operation
From the moment the sUAS becomes airborne until it is no longer airborne, broadcasting throughout the entire flight

explanations.a: The broadcast obligation is tied to the aircraft being airborne, not simply to the power state; ground-idle periods between flights may not require active broadcast depending on the system design.
explanations.b: Remote ID broadcast is required throughout all flights regardless of airspace class; it is not limited to controlled airspace operations.
explanations.c: The regulation uses the airborne condition as the trigger; while landing and stopping terminates the airborne state, the key framing under Part 89 is the airborne period.
explanations.d: Under 14 CFR 89.315, a Standard Remote ID UAS must broadcast the required Remote ID message elements from takeoff until the aircraft is no longer airborne, throughout the entire flight operation.

questions.name: Remote Identification
questions.objective: 3.2 Remote ID module (broadcast module) as compliance option
questions.keyword: broadcast module retrofit non-Standard Remote ID UAS
questions.text: A remote pilot owns an older sUAS that does not have built-in Standard Remote ID capability. The pilot wants to continue operating it outside of a FRIA. Under 14 CFR Part 89, what hardware solution allows an existing sUAS without built-in Remote ID to comply with Remote ID requirements?

answers.text: A third-party GPS logger that records flight telemetry and uploads the data to an FAA server within 24 hours of each flight
A Remote ID broadcast module — a separate device attached to the sUAS that broadcasts the required Remote ID messages during flight
An ADS-B Out transponder installed on the sUAS, which provides equivalent position broadcast capability acceptable under Part 89
A subscription to an FAA-approved Network Remote ID service that receives telemetry via cellular uplink during the operation

explanations.a: A GPS data logger that uploads data after the flight does not satisfy the real-time broadcast requirement of Part 89; Remote ID must be broadcast during the flight, not retroactively transmitted.
explanations.b: Under 14 CFR Part 89 Subpart F, a Remote ID broadcast module is an FAA-accepted device that can be attached to a non-compliant sUAS to transmit the required Remote ID messages, allowing the aircraft to operate outside a FRIA.
explanations.c: ADS-B Out is explicitly prohibited on sUAS under 14 CFR 107.67 and does not serve as a Remote ID compliance pathway under Part 89.
explanations.d: Network Remote ID is not a recognized compliance pathway under Part 89 for standard operations; the rule requires a broadcast (radio frequency) transmission, not a network-dependent uplink.

questions.name: Remote Identification
questions.text: A community-based organization that manages a model aircraft flying field wants its members to continue flying older sUAS without Remote ID capability. The organization plans to apply to the FAA for designation as a FRIA. Under 14 CFR Part 89, which entities are eligible to apply for FRIA designation?

answers.text: Only individual Part 107 remote pilots who own the property where the flying site is located
Community-based organizations recognized by the FAA and educational institutions
Any registered sUAS owner who submits an application through the FAA DroneZone portal
Only local governments and federal agencies with jurisdiction over the proposed FRIA boundaries

explanations.a: Individual remote pilots cannot apply for FRIA designation on their own; the rule limits eligibility to specific organizational types.
explanations.b: Under 14 CFR 89.210, only FAA-recognized community-based organizations (such as the Academy of Model Aeronautics) and educational institutions may apply for FRIA designation.
explanations.c: Individual sUAS owners, regardless of registration status, are not eligible applicants for FRIA designation under Part 89.
explanations.d: Local governments and federal agencies are not among the eligible FRIA applicants specified in Part 89; the rule specifies community-based organizations and educational institutions.

questions.name: Remote Identification
questions.text: A university has received FAA FRIA designation for its drone research campus. Students wish to fly older non-Remote-ID-equipped research aircraft within the FRIA boundaries. Under 14 CFR Part 89, what altitude constraint applies to sUAS operating within an FAA-Recognized Identification Area?

answers.text: No altitude restriction applies within a FRIA; aircraft may fly to any altitude permitted by other applicable FAA regulations
Operations within a FRIA must remain at or below 400 ft AGL above the FRIA boundary perimeter line
Operations within a FRIA are limited to 200 ft AGL to ensure non-compliant aircraft remain identifiable by ground observers
Operations within a FRIA must remain at or below 400 ft AGL above the ground within the FRIA boundary

explanations.a: FRIAs do impose an altitude restriction; operating without Remote ID compliance requires remaining within the defined FRIA boundaries both laterally and vertically.
explanations.b: The 400-ft limit is measured above the ground within the FRIA, not above the boundary perimeter line; lateral positioning must also remain within the FRIA.
explanations.c: 200 ft AGL is not the FRIA altitude restriction; Part 89 sets the limit at 400 ft AGL above the ground within the FRIA.
explanations.d: Under 14 CFR 89.205, sUAS operating within a FRIA without Remote ID compliance must remain within the lateral boundaries of the FRIA and at or below 400 ft AGL above the ground within the FRIA.

questions.name: Remote Identification
questions.objective: 3.4 Remote ID enforcement and operating restrictions
questions.text: During a commercial sUAS mapping flight, a remote pilot's Standard Remote ID broadcast system malfunctions and stops transmitting. The pilot is currently operating outside any FRIA. Under 14 CFR Part 89, what is the correct course of action when Remote ID broadcast capability is lost during flight?

answers.text: Continue the operation at reduced speed and notify the FAA of the malfunction within 24 hours of landing
Immediately maneuver the sUAS to a FRIA and complete the remaining mission from within that area
Land the sUAS as soon as practicable; continuing to operate without Remote ID broadcast outside a FRIA is not authorized
Reduce altitude to 100 ft AGL and proceed directly to the home point; the reduced altitude restores technical compliance

explanations.a: Continuing operations at reduced speed while broadcasting is non-functional does not satisfy Remote ID requirements; the pilot must terminate the flight.
explanations.b: Repositioning to a FRIA mid-mission may not be feasible and still requires continued flight while non-compliant; landing as soon as practicable is the required response.
explanations.c: Under 14 CFR Part 89, sUAS operating outside a FRIA must broadcast Remote ID throughout the flight; if the broadcast capability is lost, the operation cannot continue legally, and the remote pilot must land the aircraft as soon as practicable.
explanations.d: Reducing altitude does not restore Remote ID broadcast capability and does not constitute compliance; the required action is to land the aircraft.

questions.name: Remote Identification
questions.objective: 3.4 Remote ID enforcement and operating restrictions
questions.keyword: Remote ID law enforcement authorized to inspect
questions.text: A law enforcement officer approaches a remote pilot during an sUAS operation and asks to inspect the aircraft and verify Remote ID compliance. Under 14 CFR Part 107 and Part 89, which statement accurately describes the remote pilot's obligation in this situation?

answers.text: The remote pilot must immediately land the aircraft to allow inspection and present their remote pilot certificate upon request
The remote pilot may continue the flight uninterrupted and schedule a post-flight meeting with the officer at their earliest convenience
The remote pilot must verbally confirm Remote ID compliance but is not required to present the physical aircraft or any documents
The remote pilot has no obligation to cooperate with law enforcement officers who are not FAA aviation safety inspectors

explanations.a: Under 14 CFR 107.7, a remote pilot must present their remote pilot certificate for inspection upon request by an FAA representative, a federal, state, or local law enforcement officer, or any authorized representative; terminating the flight for inspection is the required response.
explanations.b: Continuing the flight and deferring to a later meeting does not satisfy the obligation to present documents upon request; the inspection obligation is immediate.
explanations.c: Verbal confirmation alone does not fulfill the inspection requirement; the remote pilot must be able to present their certificate and make the aircraft available for inspection as directed.
explanations.d: State and local law enforcement officers are among those authorized to request certificate presentation under 107.7; the obligation to cooperate is not limited to FAA inspectors.

questions.name: Remote Identification
questions.objective: 3.1 Remote ID applicability and broadcast requirements
questions.keyword: Remote ID serial number CTA 2063-A standard
questions.text: A drone manufacturer asks what serial number format the FAA requires for Remote ID broadcast purposes on Standard Remote ID UAS. Under 14 CFR Part 89, what serial number standard must be used on UAS subject to Remote ID requirements?

answers.text: Any manufacturer-assigned alphanumeric string of at least 8 characters is acceptable as long as it is unique within the manufacturer's product line
The serial number must match the aircraft's Part 48 registration number exactly as issued by the FAA upon registration
The serial number must conform to the ANSI/CTA-2063-A standard for unmanned aircraft serial numbers
The serial number must be a 6-digit numeric code assigned by the FAA at the time of Remote ID equipment approval

explanations.a: An arbitrary alphanumeric string does not satisfy the Part 89 serial number requirement; the regulation specifies compliance with the ANSI/CTA-2063-A standard.
explanations.b: The Part 48 registration number and the Remote ID serial number serve different purposes and are not required to match; the remote ID serial must conform to ANSI/CTA-2063-A.
explanations.c: Under 14 CFR 89.305, the UAS identification required for Remote ID broadcast must be a serial number that complies with the ANSI/CTA-2063-A standard for small unmanned aircraft serial numbers.
explanations.d: The FAA does not assign 6-digit Remote ID serial numbers; serial numbers are assigned by manufacturers and must conform to the ANSI/CTA-2063-A standard.

questions.name: Remote Identification
questions.objective: 3.2 Remote ID module (broadcast module) as compliance option
questions.keyword: broadcast module must not be removed in flight
questions.text: A remote pilot attaches an FAA-accepted Remote ID broadcast module to a non-compliant sUAS before flight. During a long mapping mission, battery management is a concern and the pilot considers temporarily powering off the module to extend the sUAS battery life. Under Part 89, may the pilot power down the Remote ID broadcast module during flight?

answers.text: Yes, the module may be powered off for segments of the flight that occur entirely within Class G airspace below 400 ft AGL
Yes, if a visual observer is positioned at the control station to maintain manual situational awareness during the non-broadcasting segment
No, the broadcast module must remain operational and transmitting throughout the entire duration of the flight
Yes, but only during the outbound leg of a round-trip flight when the sUAS is traveling away from populated areas

explanations.a: Airspace class does not create an exception to the continuous broadcast requirement; Remote ID must transmit throughout the entire flight regardless of airspace.
explanations.b: A visual observer's presence does not fulfill the Remote ID broadcast requirement; the module must remain active throughout the operation.
explanations.c: Under 14 CFR Part 89, a Remote ID broadcast module must broadcast the required message elements throughout the entire flight; powering it down mid-flight eliminates Remote ID compliance and is not authorized.
explanations.d: No directional or population-density exception permits pausing Remote ID broadcast during a flight; continuous transmission is required from takeoff until the aircraft is no longer airborne.
